mapping.581533_0: A toothache is a pain in or around a tooth that may be caused by: 1 Tooth decay. 2 Abscessed tooth. 3 Tooth fracture. 4 A damaged filling. 5 Repetitive motions, such as chewing gum or grinding teeth.
mapping.581533_1: Bacteria that live in your mouth thrive on the sugars and starches in the food you eat. These bacteria form a sticky plaque that clings to the surface of your teeth. Acids produced by the bacteria in plaque can eat through the hard, white coating on the outside of your teeth (enamel), creating a cavity.
mapping.581533_2: To treat your toothache, your dentist will first obtain your medical history and conduct a physical exam. He or she will ask you questions about the pain, such as when the pain started, how severe it is, where the pain is located, what makes the pain worse, and what makes it better.
mapping.581533_3: Pain around the teeth and the jaws can be symptoms of heart disease such as angina. If your dentist suspects a medical illness could be the cause of your toothache, he or she may refer you to a physician. If you have a toothache, you may have a cavity or advanced gum disease.
mapping.581533_4: A root canal might be needed if the cause of the toothache is determined to be an infection of the tooth's nerve. Bacteria that have worked their way into the inner aspects of the tooth cause such an infection. An antibiotic may be prescribed if there is fever or swelling of the jaw.
mapping.581533_5: Until you can see your dentist, try these self-care tips for a toothache: 1 Rinse your mouth with warm water. 2 Use dental floss to remove any food particles or plaque wedged between your teeth.
mapping.581533_6: Other causes of toothache can include: 1 An accumulation of food and debris between your teeth, especially if teeth have spacing between them. 2 Infection at the root of the tooth or in the gums. 3 Trauma to the tooth, including injury or grinding your teeth.
mapping.581533_7: Call your dentist immediately if you have any of the following with a toothache: 1 Pain that persists for more than a day or two. 2 Fever. 3 Signs and symptoms of infection, such as swelling, pain when you bite, red gums or a foul-tasting discharge. 4 Trouble breathing or swallowing.
mapping.581533_8: While tooth decay is often the primary cause of a toothache, it's important for you to have a complete oral examination to determine the cause. Other causes of a toothache can include the following: 1 Infection. 2 Gum disease. 3 Grinding teeth (bruxism). 4 Tooth trauma. 5 An abnormal bite.
mapping.581533_9: See your dentist as soon as possible about your toothache if: 1 You have a toothache that lasts longer than 1 or 2 days. 2 Your toothache is severe. 3 You have a fever, earache, or pain upon opening your mouth wide.

mapping.1164704_1: Learn the causes and symptoms of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease as it is the most common liver disease in the world now. It affects even children. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease has been recognized as a silent, yet major, disease in developed countries. It starts with a simple fatty liver and gradually advances to fibrosis. The final stage is cirrhosis and liver failure. The symptoms are vague throughout the stages.
mapping.1164704_2: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the build up of extra fat in liver cells that is not caused by alcohol. It is normal for the liver to contain some fat. However, if more than 5% – 10% percent of the liver’s weight is fat, then it is called a fatty liver (steatosis).
mapping.1164704_3: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease is initially suspected if blood tests show high levels of liver enzymes. However, other liver diseases are first ruled out through additional tests. Often, an ultrasound is used to confirm the Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease diagnosis.
mapping.1164704_4: There are a few lesser known causes of NAFLD, or some medical conditions that could aggravate a fatty liver. 1 Sleep apnea. 2 Polycystic ovarian disease (PCOD) 3 Viral hepatitis. 4 Medical issues that flare up during pregnancy like autoimmune hepatitis. 5 Underactive thyroid.
